title: Aggregation drops distinct metrics and events when deduplication keys collide
description:
During daily-to-monthly aggregation in devrel-io, distinct rows are being dropped because the aggregation deduplication keys do not include the full grain of the records.

* `dedupKey()` omits `target`, so metrics for different targets collide when their source, project, metric, date, and extra fields match. This dropped eight RSS `total_items` snapshots from July 2026, including four of the five initial feed snapshots.
* `dedupEventKey()` omits `target` and `ref`, so events on different issues can collide when their source, project, type, timestamp, user, and extra fields match. This dropped nine GitHub events from the same compaction.

I found this by comparing devrel-io immediately before and after July was compacted (`f6e38e13` to `3bfff9ba`). Two concrete cases:

```text
rss | open-source-website | total_items | 2026-07-27
```

Five rows shared those fields but represented different feeds: blog, people, events, resources, and software. Because `target` was omitted, only one survived.

Likewise, GitHub events such as:

```text
github | vip | issue_close | same timestamp | same user
```

could refer to different issue numbers. Because `ref` was omitted, one issue-close event was retained and another discarded.

 I _think_ the metric key should include `target`, while the event key should include both `target` and `ref`.
